key_insight: Combining a large, high-quality real-world benchmark (ZEDD) with a purpose-built network (FOSSA) enables reliable zero-shot depth-from-defocus estimation—producing accurate metric depth on unseen scenes without dataset-specific fine-tuning.
problem_solved: Overfitting of Depth-from-Defocus models to narrow datasets; lack of a large, realistic benchmark and architectures designed for zero-shot generalization across real-world scenes and camera setups.
method: Release ZEDD: a new real-world DfD benchmark with ~8.3× more scenes and substantially higher-quality images and ground-truth depth than prior datasets.
Design FOSSA: a novel network architecture engineered to aggregate focus-stack cues and predict dense metric depth with strong zero-shot generalization.
Adopt training/evaluation practices that prioritize cross-dataset zero-shot performance to validate robustness on unseen scenes and devices.
impact: Enables development and fair benchmarking of DfD models that generalize to new cameras and environments—accelerating practical deployment in robotics, AR, and computational photography. ZEDD provides a stronger standard dataset for future research.
